text: Harness: explicit stage machine in loop-worker with structured output per stage
description: Split runCycle (one streamText with 10 steps) into stages: orient -> decompose | execute -> verify -> reflect -> record. Each stage: own role model, own compiled context, own tool set, own step budget, and a zod-validated result (generateObject) that the harness applies to the graph itself, so graph writes are deterministic code, not model tool calls. Leaf test decides decompose vs execute (open leaf with estimated cost under the per-cycle budget -> execute). Stage transitions are logged as loop events so the loop panel shows where a cycle is. Learned from f3231c4c: once a decision is settled, do not ask a model to re-decide it.

status.comment: loop-worker runCycle is now a stage machine (packages/loop-worker/src/cycle.ts, transitions in stages.ts): orient → decompose (containers) | execute (open leaves) → verify → reflect → record; execute 'too_large' decomposes in the same cycle once. Each stage ends with a zod-validated submit_* tool call (stage-runner.ts; works on any tool-calling provider, one retry turn with only the submit tool if the model stops without submitting). Stages get their own tool subsets and step budgets; models never get graph-write tools, the harness applies results through the MCP handlers (graph-writes.ts). Stage transitions are loop events and the activity line. Evidence: loop-worker tests 16/16 (stages, runner with MockLanguageModelV3, full cycle with fake graph), backend loop-cycle e2e 3/3 (real backend + spawned worker + fake HTTP model incl. human-wait), backend 159/159, knip clean. Still one model for all stages until the role registry (e6bd3fd6).
